It is these classic Wörthersee moments that make a stay by the lake so special: an early morning swim near Kapuziner Island, freshly caught whitefish enjoyed by the water at lunchtime, and a leisurely cycle ride past historic villas and lakeside lidos in Pörtschach or Velden in the afternoon. Lake Wörthersee combines a summer holiday in Carinthia with swimming, water sports and destinations that have long been associated with summer relaxation.
Around the lake, promenades lead to cafés, lakeside terraces and bathing spots, while attractions such as the Pyramidenkogel observation tower, Minimundus and cruises on Lake Wörthersee can easily be combined with a day by the water.
Between Klagenfurt, Maria Wörth and Velden, the lakeside lifestyle comes into its own. Spend the day stand-up paddleboarding, wakeboarding or sailing, then enjoy an evening stroll along the promenade or a sundowner at a bar by the water. Events such as Starnacht am Wörthersee, Namaste am See and the See.Ess.Spiele culinary festival add to the atmosphere, bringing together food, activities and relaxed summer days by the lake.
Lake Wörthersee enchants with its turquoise-blue water and idyllic location, making it a popular destination for relaxation and water sports.
The lido features a wide sandy beach, a 113-metre-long water slide with a timer, three jetties and spacious sunbathing areas with views of the Pyramidenkogel.
Business Beach offers workspaces by the lake with Wi-Fi, power sockets, shade and lockers, as well as views of Veldener Bay.
The lido (with beach club & lakeside restaurant) is situated on the shores of Lake Wörthersee: water sports, boat hire & culinary delights in exclusive lakeside setting.
This bathing beach covers around 20,000 m² of sunbathing lawns with mature trees, access to the lake, and a wide range of sports and swimming facilities.
The water park features an island accessible via a 100-metre-long arched bridge, around 15,000 m² of sunbathing area and a 75-metre-long water slide.
With 2 km of lakeside promenade, magnificent villas and historic charm, Pörtschach am Wörthersee is characterised by its lakeside setting and spa architecture.
Boutique hotels, lakeside terraces, and bars are a defining feature of Velden's townscape – particularly during the summer months along the lakeside promenade.
The church island of Maria Wörth is one of the most famous spots on Lake Wörthersee – with lake views, a wedding chapel and peaceful paths along the peninsula.
Lakeside terraces, beach clubs, bars and restaurants shape the culinary scene around Lake Wörthersee. Mediterranean flavours meet Carinthian cuisine, while dining by the water and sundowners with lake views create memorable moments throughout the summer.
Among the region's culinary highlights are Restaurant Rosé in Velden, known for its fish specialities and lakeside setting, and Restaurant Seespitz , where fine dining with two toques is served directly on the waterfront. In Maria Wörth, Gourmet Restaurant Hubert Wallner , awarded one Michelin star, is one of Austria's leading gourmet destinations. In Klagenfurt, Restaurant Maria Loretto enjoys a unique location on a peninsula, with a spacious terrace overlooking the lake.
Food lovers can also experience the lake through the See.Ess.Spiele festival series, where guest chefs create special dining experiences at exceptional locations around Lake Wörthersee.
The distinctive colour is caused by the high calcium carbonate content, the depth of the lake and the scattering of light in the water – depending on its composition, it ranges from pale green to the characteristic turquoise blue.
At the turn of the century, the aristocracy and the middle classes moved from their city mansions to their country summer residences. This pleasant tradition has a name in Austria: ‘Sommerfrische’. It was this tradition that drew Johannes Brahms, Gustav Mahler and Alban Berg to Lake Wörthersee.
Lining the Blumenpromenade are the elegant Belle Époque villas, whose distinctive architecture continues to shape the character of Lake Wörthersee to this day.
Prehistoric pile dwellings and artefacts dating from the 4th millennium BC have been discovered in the area around Kapuziner Island. The island has been a nature reserve since 1966.
The 58.5-kilometre circular walking route takes you around Lake Wörthersee in four stages – past castles, through forests and with views of the Karawanken mountains.
Located on the eastern bay of Lake Wörthersee, the Lendspitz-Maiernigg Natura 2000 site is a protected habitat for numerous animal and plant species and one of Klagenfurt's most valuable natural areas. Reed beds, wetlands and lakeside paths create a diverse landscape that combines nature with close proximity to the city.
Walking and cycling routes follow the shoreline into the eastern bay of Lake Wörthersee, passing quiet inlets, jetties and birdwatching spots. The protected area provides an important refuge for wildlife and is considered one of the key conservation areas in the Alpe-Adria region.
Despite its peaceful setting, the nature reserve is only a few minutes from Europapark, Klagenfurt lido and the city centre. Lendspitz is particularly popular for walking, jogging and cycling, offering an easy escape into nature right on the edge of the city.
Lake Wörthersee in Carinthia is known for its warm water temperatures of up to 27°C, its many lakeside lidos and its relaxed southern atmosphere. Destinations such as Velden, Pörtschach and Klagenfurt combine swimming with excellent dining, water sports and cycling opportunities.
The event calendar around Lake Wörthersee includes the yoga festival Namaste am See , the Pink Lake LGBTQ+ Festival and Starnacht am Wörthersee . Sporting highlights include Kärnten Läuft , the Wörthersee Marathon and the Gravel Race , while cultural events such as the Carinthian Crime Fiction Festival and the Days of German-Language Literature attract visitors from across the region.
Lake Wörthersee is easily accessible by train, car and plane. International rail connections serve Klagenfurt, Velden and Pörtschach. The new Koralm Railway links Graz and Klagenfurt in around 42 minutes. By road, the A2 Southern Motorway connects the region with Vienna, Graz and Italy. Klagenfurt Airport is the closest airport, while Ljubljana Airport is just around 87 kilometres away. Local public transport, cycling routes and Lake Wörthersee's passenger boats make it easy to travel between destinations around the lake.
Numerous lidos line the shores of Lake Wörthersee, including Klagenfurt Lido , Promenadenbad Pörtschach and Velden Lido . Sunbathing lawns, bathing jetties and direct lake access make them popular places to enjoy the water throughout the summer.
The main season for swimming and water sports runs from May to September. Warm summer temperatures and water temperatures of up to 27°C make this the ideal time to enjoy the lake. Spring and autumn are particularly well suited to cycling, walking and relaxed days by the water.
Lake Wörthersee offers a wide range of water-based activities. Swimming, stand-up paddleboarding, sailing and kayaking are among the most popular options, alongside water skiing, wakeboarding and boat hire available around the lake.

Wörthersee ( German pronunciation: [ ˈvœʁtɐˌzeː ] ⓘ ; Slovene : Vrbsko jezero , English: Lake Wörth [ 1 ] [ 2 ] [ 3 ] ) is a lake in the southern Austrian state of Carinthia . The bathing lake is a main tourist destination in summer.
Wörthersee is Carinthia's largest lake. It is elongated, about 16.5 km (10.3 mi) long and 1.5 km (0.93 mi) wide, and stretches from the outskirts of the Carinthian capital Klagenfurt in the east to the bay of Velden in the west. Situated within the Klagenfurt Basin, its shores are flanked to the north and south by the foothills of the Gurktal Alps and the Karawanks range, all covered with dense forests beyond which snow-capped Alpine peaks are visible. The lake's water is of a distinctive blue-green colour and transparent.
Lake Wörth and its basin in the central Carinthian foothills were largely formed by glaciers during the last ice age . The lake is divided into three basins by several islands and peninsulas. The western basin stretches from Velden to Pörtschach , the central basin from Pörtschach to Maria Wörth and the eastern basin from Maria Wörth to Klagenfurt. Numerous brooks flow into the lake; its sole outlet is the Glanfurt river in the east, eventually flowing into the Drava (Drau) river via the Glan and Gurk tributaries.
The northern shore is densely built up with the main resort towns of Krumpendorf , Pörtschach, and Velden. The Süd Autobahn motorway and a railway mainline occupy the narrow space between the steep hills and the shore. The southern shore is quieter and less developed.
The water surface ( epilimnion ) can reach up to 25 °C in summer. In winter, the region is often covered by snow and approximately every 10 years the lake freezes over, attracting numerous ice skaters. Lake Wörth's fauna is dominated by fish typically found in alpine lakes. The most common species are the pike ( Esox lucius ) and the common whitefish ( Coregonus lavaretus ).
First mentioned as Werdse in an 1143 deed, the lake's name originates from the islands in the lake, most notably Maria Wörth, a peninsula since the building of the Glanfurt outlet in 1770. Other islands are Schlangeninsel and Kapuzinerinsel; the former island of Maria Loretto is today also a peninsula. Until the 19th century the lake was called "Werdersee"  (cf. Old High German weride : "island" or " ait "), i.e. "Island Lake", but also Klagenfurt Lake or Velden Lake (as in Slovene: Vrbsko jezero ).
In the early 19th century the marshy shores were home only to a handful of poor peasants. The opening of the Austrian Southern Railway line ( Südbahn ) to Klagenfurt in 1863, later extended to Villach along the northern shore, quickly turned the Wörthersee into an exclusive summer retreat for Vienna 's nobility and wealthy bourgeoisie. Especially Velden and Pörtschach developed to main tourist resorts.
Up to today, the Mediterranean climate and the clean, warm waters make Lake Wörth a popular tourist destination in summer. Although the region around the lake has been termed "Austria's Monte Carlo", in recent decades tourism around Lake Wörthersee has suffered from tough competition from package holidays to cheaper overseas destinations. As a response a number of local businesses have tried to focus on niches such as high quality tourism, family tourism or golf and horse-riding vacations.
Most tourists visit the Lake in the months of July and August when water temperatures reach 25 °C. A large proportion of visitors return every summer and some own or rent holiday homes along the shore. The vast majority of visitors come from Vienna, northern Germany and the Netherlands .
The largest Volkswagen and Audi car show in Europe, the Wörthersee GTI-Treffen (in English, "Wörthersee Meeting" or simply "Wörthersee"), has been held in the lakeside town of Reifnitz (usually in May) every year from 1982 to 2021 (the 2022 event was cancelled due to the organisational problems). The municipality have announced in February 2023 that no GTI-Treffen would be permitted anymore. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] The organisers issued the statement: "the effects of climate change, the responsibility of political decision-makers for the preservation of ecosystems, and the need to align actions at all levels according to the principles of sustainability make it necessary to place the future design under new premises. On the basis of these considerations, we can state the municipality of Maria Worth will no longer host any conventional major automotive events in the next few years." [ 6 ]
The A2 Süd Autobahn motorway ( European Route E66 ) from Vienna to Italy passes along the northern side of the lake, as does the B83 Kärntner Straße highway connecting Klagenfurt with Villach and the Südbahn railway line from Vienna to Venice . There is also a cycle path along the northern shore. In summer, passenger boats connect the largest settlements. The number of private speedboats is strictly limited by a quota system to limit the environmental damage and hazard to swimmers.
